key_insight: The paper turns numeric tabular datasets into comparable statistical embeddings, enabling retrieval and interpretable cross-dataset alignment even when feature names and conventions differ.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to match unknown datasets to prior examples for data-driven model selection, simulation initialization, and retrieval-augmented workflows.
method: Compute structured exploratory-data-analysis descriptors for each dataset.
Embed descriptors into a shared vector space with a pretrained sentence transformer, then measure similarity with CCA.
Use penalized CCA to recover sparse, interpretable variable-level correspondences; optionally add differential privacy before embedding.
evidence_signal: Across 15 datasets, the method achieved a total P@1 of 0.9, with nearest-neighbor retrieval and clustering remaining robust under embedding ablations and differential privacy budgets.
watch_item: Descriptor quality, CCA sparsity settings, and privacy budget choices may materially affect alignment stability and interpretability on new datasets.
paper_title: Statistical Embeddings for Similarity, Retrieval, and Interpretable Alignment of Numeric Tabular Datasets
